name: Little Round Top
desc: Rocky hill on the Union left flank.

name: George Meade
desc: Commander of the Army of Potomac. This was headquarters of Meade at the Leister house during Gettysburg battle. The house was damaged by the cannon fire.

name: Robert E. Lee
desc: Commander of the Army of Northern Virginia.

name: Big Round Top
desc: Highest hill on the battlefield.

name: Reynolds Woods
desc: Woodlot west of Gettysburg where some of the fiercest first-day fighting occurred. General Reynolds was mortally wounded nearby.

name: Trostle Farm
desc: Farmstead near the Peach Orchard that witnessed intense fighting on July 2. The barn still bears artillery damage.

name: Codori Farm
desc: Farm located near the center of Pickett's Charge. Confederate troops crossed its fields during the assault.

name: Bryan Farm
desc: Property situated behind portions of the Union line on Cemetery Ridge and associated with Federal defensive positions.

name: Ziegler's Grove
desc: Small grove of trees near the Union center. The area became a focal point during Pickett's Charge.

name: Cemetery Ridge
desc: Backbone of the Union defensive line. The ridge stretched south from Cemetery Hill and played a central role throughout the battle.

name: Powers Hill
desc: Important Union artillery position supporting the right flank near Culp's Hill.

name: Benner's Hill
desc: Confederate artillery position east of Gettysburg. Batteries here exchanged fire with Union guns on Cemetery Hill.

name: East Cavalry Field
desc: Site of the major cavalry battle fought between Stuart's Confederate cavalry and Union horsemen under Gregg and Custer on July 3.

name: Farnsworth's Charge
desc: Union cavalry assault launched late on July 3 against Confederate positions near Big Round Top. The attack suffered heavy losses.

name: Pickett's Charge
desc: Massive Confederate assault on July 3 involving divisions under Pickett, Pettigrew, and Trimble. It ended in a costly Confederate defeat.

name: Gettysburg National Cemetery
desc: Final resting place for Union soldiers killed in the battle and the site of Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address.

name: Abraham Lincoln
desc: Sixteenth President of the United States. Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at the cemetery dedication on November 19, 1863.

name: James Longstreet
desc: Lee's senior corps commander. Longstreet directed major Confederate attacks against the Union left flank on July 2 and expressed reservations about the July 3 assault that became known as Pickett's Charge.

name: Winfield Scott Hancock
desc: Commander of the Union II Corps. Hancock helped organize Union defenses on Cemetery Ridge and played a critical role in holding the center of the Federal line.

name: John Reynolds
desc: One of the Union Army's most respected leaders. Reynolds was killed early on July 1 while directing troops north and west of Gettysburg.

name: John Buford
desc: Union cavalry commander whose troopers delayed Confederate forces on July 1, buying time for Union infantry to reach and defend the high ground south of town.

name: Richard S. Ewell
desc: Commander of the Confederate Second Corps. Ewell's forces attacked Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill and have long been associated with debates over the first day's fighting.

name: J.E.B. Stuart
desc: Commander of Confederate cavalry. Stuart arrived late during the Gettysburg Campaign and fought an important cavalry engagement east of Gettysburg on July 3.

name: George Pickett
desc: Confederate division commander whose troops formed a major component of the July 3 assault remembered as Pickett's Charge.

name: Cemetery Hill
desc: A key Union strongpoint and artillery platform. Cemetery Hill formed the center of the famous fishhook-shaped Union defensive line throughout the battle.

name: Devil's Den
desc: A dramatic field of massive boulders southwest of Little Round Top. Fierce fighting occurred here on July 2 during Longstreet's attack.

name: The Wheatfield
desc: Scene of repeated attacks and counterattacks on July 2. The area changed hands several times and became one of the bloodiest locations on the battlefield.

name: Peach Orchard
desc: The advanced position occupied by General Sickles' corps. Confederate attacks shattered the salient and contributed to severe Union losses.

name: Culp's Hill
desc: Wooded hill anchoring the Union right flank. Intense combat occurred here on July 2 and July 3 as Confederate forces attempted to turn the Federal line.

name: Reynolds Woods
desc: Woodlot west of Gettysburg where some of the fiercest first-day fighting occurred. General Reynolds was mortally wounded nearby.

name: Trostle Farm
desc: Farmstead near the Peach Orchard that witnessed intense fighting on July 2. The barn still bears artillery damage.

name: Codori Farm
desc: Farm located near the center of Pickett's Charge. Confederate troops crossed its fields during the assault.

name: Bryan Farm
desc: Property situated behind portions of the Union line on Cemetery Ridge and associated with Federal defensive positions.

name: Ziegler's Grove
desc: Small grove of trees near the Union center. The area became a focal point during Pickett's Charge.

name: Cemetery Ridge
desc: Backbone of the Union defensive line. The ridge stretched south from Cemetery Hill and played a central role throughout the battle.

name: Powers Hill
desc: Important Union artillery position supporting the right flank near Culp's Hill.

name: Benner's Hill
desc: Confederate artillery position east of Gettysburg. Batteries here exchanged fire with Union guns on Cemetery Hill.

name: East Cavalry Field
desc: Site of the major cavalry battle fought between Stuart's Confederate cavalry and Union horsemen under Gregg and Custer on July 3.

name: Farnsworth's Charge
desc: Union cavalry assault launched late on July 3 against Confederate positions near Big Round Top. The attack suffered heavy losses.

name: A. P. Hill
desc: Commanded the Confederate Third Corps. His troops initiated the fighting west of Gettysburg on July 1 and played major roles throughout the battle.

name: Oliver O. Howard
desc: Commander of the Union XI Corps. He helped establish the Union defensive position centered on Cemetery Hill.

name: Daniel Sickles
desc: Union III Corps commander. His controversial advance to the Peach Orchard created a vulnerable salient in the Union line.

name: Lewis Armistead
desc: Confederate brigadier general who crossed the stone wall during Pickett's Charge before being mortally wounded.

name: John Gibbon
desc: Union division commander whose troops helped repel Pickett's Charge and hold the center of Cemetery Ridge.

name: Henry Heth
desc: Confederate division commander whose movement toward Gettysburg on July 1 helped trigger the battle.

name: Abner Doubleday
desc: Union I Corps commander after Reynolds' death. Directed forces resisting Confederate attacks on the first day.

name: Little Round Top Monument Area
desc: Cluster of monuments marking the regiments that defended Little Round Top during fighting on July 2.

name: Virginia Monument
desc: Features a prominent equestrian statue of Robert E. Lee and honors Virginia soldiers who fought at Gettysburg.

name: Eternal Light Peace Memorial
desc: Dedicated in 1938 during the reunion of Union and Confederate veterans as a symbol of national reconciliation.

name: 72nd Pennsylvania Monument
desc: One of Gettysburg's most recognizable monuments, located near the Angle and the High Water Mark.

name: High Water Mark Memorial
desc: Marks the symbolic furthest advance of Confederate forces during Pickett's Charge on July 3.

name: The Angle
desc: A bend in the stone wall on Cemetery Ridge that became the focal point of Pickett's Charge.

name: Seminary Ridge
desc: Major Confederate position west of Gettysburg. Lee observed much of the battle from this ridge.

name: McPherson Ridge
desc: Location of intense fighting on July 1 where Buford's cavalry delayed advancing Confederate forces.

name: Herr Ridge
desc: Western ridge crossed by Confederate troops approaching Gettysburg during the opening stages of the battle.

name: Rose Woods
desc: Wooded area between Devil's Den and the Wheatfield that witnessed fierce close-range combat.

name: Plum Run
desc: Small stream in the valley between Devil's Den and the Round Tops, sometimes called the Valley of Death.

name: Spangler's Spring
desc: Important water source near Culp's Hill and the site of notable fighting on the Union right flank.

name: Joshua Chamberlain
desc: Commander of the 20th Maine.

name: Pennsylvania Memorial
desc: Largest state memorial.
